claim: This contract proves the named local kernel and architecture checks only. It records, but does not fabricate, the durable runtime, authoritative lineage, and maintenance guarantees still required for promotion.

evidence_classes.ci_now: Executable source or test evidence available in this repository now.
evidence_classes.runtime_required: Evidence that requires a concrete durable adapter, concurrency, restart, or crash injection.
evidence_classes.external_required: Evidence that requires an independently administered trust root or deployment boundary.
evidence_classes.declaration_only: A checked declaration of an absent guarantee; it can never establish PASS.

profiles.target: Converged extension and kernel maintenance surface

capabilities.title: Immutable deterministic transition reducer

evidence.claim: One generic reducer handles unrelated caller vocabularies without profile data.
Exact replay is idempotent and evaluator or policy drift fails closed.

capabilities.falsifier: Identical value inputs produce different transition results, or a conflicting event identity overwrites accepted history.
capabilities.solution: Keep step as a pure value reducer and extend behavior through versioned values and injected ports.
acceptance: Repeated identical inputs are value-identical.
Replay never advances accepted history.
Policy mismatch returns an unchanged snapshot.

capabilities.title: Exact-version canonical receipt integrity

evidence.claim: Canonical v1 receipts round-trip and bind their terminal definition path.
A self-consistent unknown receipt schema is rejected instead of interpreted as v1.

capabilities.falsifier: An unsupported schema version parses, or an edited v1 receipt retains valid local integrity.
capabilities.solution: Keep v1 exact and introduce future wire formats through explicit parsers and migration policy.
acceptance: Only the exact canonical v1 shape parses through the v1 parser.
Unknown schema versions fail with a stable error.
The content digest and declared path are recomputed during validation.

capabilities.title: Reducer-aligned structural FSM analysis

evidence.claim: Executable reachability and dead declared transitions are reported deterministically.
Terminal outgoing rules are not mistaken for executable edges.
The published invalid-event metadata matches actual reducer ordering.

capabilities.falsifier: A declared terminal, recovery, or unreachable edge is analyzed differently from step admission semantics.
capabilities.solution: Keep analysis opt-in and structural; never infer validator satisfiability or impose domain liveness rules.
acceptance: Unreachable states and executable dead transitions are identified.
Terminal outgoing and denied recovery rules are identified.
Partial transition functions and legitimate cycles remain allowed.

capabilities.title: Structurally validated local successor

evidence.claim: A fabricated terminal snapshot with an impossible empty path cannot start a successor.
A valid local successor advances exactly one bounded generation.

capabilities.falsifier: A structurally invalid or nonterminal snapshot starts another generation.
capabilities.solution: Retain this helper for local integrity only; authoritative succession belongs to the versioned lineage and authenticated-envelope capabilities.
acceptance: The predecessor can emit a structurally valid terminal receipt.
Generation advances exactly once within the configured bound.
Documentation does not call this durable or authenticated lineage.

capabilities.title: Functional core and extension boundary

evidence.claim: Every shipped module is classified and exact pure modules remain behind the declared dependency boundary.

capabilities.falsifier: A new module is silently unclassified, a pure module gains ambient effects, or domain vocabulary enters the generic core.
capabilities.solution: Keep configuration at composition boundaries and add generic pure modules to the exact architecture contract before merge.
acceptance: Every shipped module has one reviewed layer.
Pure modules pass direct syntax and responsibility ratchets.
Optional domain extensions remain outside the base wheel.

capabilities.title: Machine-checked honest claim boundary

evidence.claim: Profile readiness is derived from capability evidence and unresolved work stays visible.

capabilities.falsifier: The contract declares a profile ready while a required capability is not PASS, or a PASS claim lacks executable evidence.
capabilities.solution: Derive profile status, fail on unknown fields, and require each PASS to retain an executable evidence symbol.
acceptance: Core readiness is derived as READY.
Maintainability, runtime, and authority remain NOT_READY until their blockers pass.
Unsupported contract drift fails closed.

capabilities.title: Version-negotiated CLI extension activation
capabilities.falsifier: The CLI advertises an extension name but cannot resolve an explicitly installed provider, or loads unrequested providers.
capabilities.solution: Add a frozen extension descriptor with API version and an explicit lazy entry-point resolver; activate only requested names and keep direct injected legacy providers compatible.
acceptance: Requested installed providers activate through the CLI.
Unrequested providers are never imported.
Unsupported API versions fail before provider invocation.
Entry-point order cannot change composed check order.

capabilities.title: Generic and mutation-kernel conformance surface
capabilities.falsifier: Two similarly named kernels silently diverge on shared replay, identity-conflict, terminal, or budget semantics.
capabilities.solution: Define a small generic reducer conformance protocol and parameterized invariant suite; keep mutation-specific effects and vocabulary in its extension.
acceptance: Both kernels publish supported conformance capabilities.
Shared invariants run through adapter fixtures.
The distinct public event types fail substitution explicitly.
No mutation vocabulary moves into the generic kernel.

capabilities.title: Workflow-scoped event and predecessor lineage
capabilities.falsifier: An event created for one workflow, generation, or material revision is accepted by another, or a successor cannot name its exact predecessor.
capabilities.solution: Introduce versioned event and successor envelopes binding workflow ID, generation, material revision, expected revision, policy digest, and predecessor receipt digest without changing v1 hashes.
acceptance: Every lineage field participates in the v2 intent digest.
Cross-workflow, cross-generation, and stale-revision events fail closed.
A successor names one validated predecessor digest.
V1 remains explicitly local and unscoped.

capabilities.title: Replayable evaluator decision records
capabilities.falsifier: The same accepted event replays differently because evaluator inputs, outputs, versions, or external facts were not retained.
capabilities.solution: Record canonical validator and completion inputs, typed outputs, evaluator digest, and external fact references as accepted decision evidence; replay consumes records rather than ambient state.
acceptance: Evaluator behavior is version and digest bound.
All nondeterministic inputs are captured or explicitly marked live-only.
Offline replay reconstructs the accepted decision without network, clock, or randomness.

capabilities.title: Receipt-complete semantic replay
capabilities.falsifier: A receipt declares an admissible path but lacks the canonical event payload or completion decision needed to reproduce it.
capabilities.solution: Define receipt v2 with accepted event envelopes, decision records, completion evidence, predecessor identity, and a replay validator; preserve the v1 integrity-only parser.
acceptance: Every accepted transition can reconstruct its event.
Completion evidence is independently rechecked during replay.
Tampering with payload, decision, or lineage changes receipt identity.
Historical v1 receipts have an explicit compatibility outcome.

capabilities.title: Total loop and no-progress bounds
capabilities.falsifier: Rejected or replayed invocations continue forever without consuming any total, retry, deadline, cost, or no-progress budget.
capabilities.solution: Add an immutable runtime LoopPolicy covering total invocations, retries, corrections, no-progress streak, deadline, cost, tool calls, and cancellation with one boundary check per iteration.
acceptance: Every invocation consumes a total bound.
No-progress and retry exhaustion terminate explicitly.
Deadline and cancellation are checked before effects and after waits.
Configured bounds are stored in checkpoints and receipts.

capabilities.title: Typed terminal outcomes and recovery policy
capabilities.falsifier: Budget exhaustion or cancellation is only an exception or transient rejection and cannot be durably distinguished from success or failure.
capabilities.solution: Define completed, rejected, cancelled, exhausted, failed, and quarantined terminal outcomes with retryability, reason, last checkpoint, and pending-effect state.
acceptance: Every run ends in one typed terminal outcome or a durable runnable state.
Retryable and permanent failures are distinct.
Cancellation and exhaustion produce receipts without claiming completion.

capabilities.title: Durable append-only command and event journal
capabilities.falsifier: An acknowledged append disappears after process death, a torn record replays, or two events occupy one workflow revision.
capabilities.solution: Implement a real append-only adapter with checksummed canonical records, unique workflow sequence, durable acknowledgement, and replay from revision zero.
acceptance: Acknowledged records survive immediate process termination.
Torn or checksum-invalid tails are quarantined.
Full replay reconstructs the exact snapshot and receipt identity.
In-memory mocks do not count as durability evidence.

capabilities.title: Generation-aware compare-and-swap authority
capabilities.falsifier: Two writers commit the same next revision, or revision reset across generations creates an ABA acceptance.
capabilities.solution: CAS on workflow ID, generation, expected revision, policy/schema version, and fencing epoch in the same transaction as journal state.
acceptance: Concurrent writers produce at most one winner.
Stale generation and stale revision conflicts are typed.
Journal head and materialized revision remain equal after restart.

capabilities.title: Atomic inbox, state commit, and effect outbox
capabilities.falsifier: State commits without its effect intent, an effect exists without an accepted transition, or a duplicate command adds another journal row.
capabilities.solution: Transactionally deduplicate command identity and commit the accepted event, new snapshot, terminal outcome, and outbox intents together.
acceptance: Crash injection observes either none or all transactional records.
Identical duplicate commands return the prior result.
Conflicting duplicate identities fail permanently.
Committed undelivered effects are discoverable after restart.

capabilities.title: Durable effect idempotency and delivery accounting
capabilities.falsifier: One committed effect is logically applied twice, silently lost, or retried forever after an ambiguous acknowledgement.
capabilities.solution: Bind each effect key to canonical intent, causation, and ordinal; use idempotent or explicitly guarded adapters and persist delivery attempts and outcomes.
acceptance: Same key and intent is one logical application.
Same key with different intent is a permanent conflict.
Only classified transient failures retry.
Guarded non-idempotent effects expose reconciliation state.

capabilities.title: Versioned checkpoints and deterministic resume
capabilities.falsifier: Resume skips or repeats an accepted transition, or a corrupt newest checkpoint becomes authoritative.
capabilities.solution: Store checksummed versioned checkpoints bound to workflow, generation, revision, policy, schema, and journal position; replay the suffix after validation.
acceptance: Checkpoint plus suffix equals full replay.
Corrupt newest checkpoints fall back safely.
Restart from every state preserves the next admissible behavior.

capabilities.title: Single-writer lease with fencing
capabilities.falsifier: A stale owner commits after takeover or two workers concurrently mutate one workflow.
capabilities.solution: Lease workflow ownership through a durable authority and attach a monotonically increasing fencing epoch to every state and outbox write.
acceptance: Only one unexpired owner writes a workflow.
Stale fencing epochs are rejected after takeover.
Correctness does not rely only on a client wall clock.

capabilities.title: Explicit schema evolution and compatibility
capabilities.falsifier: Historical durable bytes cannot be classified, an upcast changes across runs, or migration leaves mixed authoritative versions.
capabilities.solution: Create a compatibility registry for event, decision, snapshot, checkpoint, and receipt versions with deterministic upcasters and golden historical fixtures.
acceptance: Every durable version is current, upcastable, read-only, or rejected.
Upcasters use no ambient clock, network, randomness, or mutable configuration.
Interrupted migrations resume idempotently or roll back.

capabilities.title: Startup and continuous reconciliation
capabilities.falsifier: Repeated reconciliation mutates healthy state, loses committed work, or resurrects stale ownership.
capabilities.solution: Implement an idempotent reconciler for journal/checkpoint drift, abandoned leases, pending effects, terminal receipts, schema state, and quarantined ambiguity.
acceptance: Healthy repeated reconciliation is a no-op.
Pending committed effects are resumed without logical duplication.
Irreparable ambiguity is quarantined with an observable reason.
Terminal state and receipt publication converge.

capabilities.title: End-to-end crash and concurrency fault matrix
capabilities.falsifier: Any durable boundary permits silent loss, split-brain ownership, duplicate logical effects, or unbounded recovery.
capabilities.solution: After the real runtime exists, inject process death before and after every durable write, effect call, acknowledgement, lease renewal, checkpoint, migration, and receipt publication boundary.
acceptance: Every fault point preserves contiguous accepted history.
Every committed effect is pending or delivered with one intent.
Stale owners cannot write after takeover.
Recovery reaches runnable, terminal, durably failed, or quarantined within a bound.

capabilities.title: Backpressure, cancellation, and observability
capabilities.falsifier: Overload grows queues without bound, cancellation races effects invisibly, or operators cannot identify a stuck workflow and pending effects.
capabilities.solution: Add bounded queues and admission policy, durable cancellation commands, structured metrics and traces, and an operator query surface keyed by workflow and causation identity.
acceptance: Queue and concurrency limits reject or defer overload explicitly.
Cancellation is idempotent and observed at safe boundaries.
Metrics expose age, no-progress, retries, lease epoch, and pending effects.
Logs and traces carry workflow, generation, command, event, and effect identities.

capabilities.title: Authenticated producer and receipt envelope
capabilities.falsifier: A producer rewrites a receipt and recomputes its unkeyed hash, or the verifier and evidence store share an unacknowledged authority.
capabilities.solution: Wrap exact canonical receipt bytes in a detached attestation verified by an injected trust-root port; record authority identity, algorithm, key version, and external anchor without embedding deployment secrets.
acceptance: Receipt integrity and producer authenticity are reported separately.
Unknown, revoked, or wrong-context authorities fail closed.
Trust-root selection remains deployment-owned.
No secret or domain authority is hard-coded in the generic package.

remediation_sequence.exit: The base framework has explicit extension negotiation and both kernels share a domain-neutral conformance suite.
Versioned identities, decisions, loop limits, outcomes, and the optional trust envelope are frozen before durable storage.
Receipt v2 can reconstruct and revalidate every accepted decision while v1 compatibility stays explicit.
One concrete adapter durably stores canonical ordered commands, events, decisions, and outcomes.
Concurrent commands have one generation-aware authoritative commit winner.
Commands, state, outcomes, and effects commit atomically under bounded observable operation.
Effect retries are durable, classified, bounded, and logically idempotent.
Resume and owner takeover preserve exact behavior and reject stale writers.
Historical durable schemas have deterministic tested compatibility outcomes.
Startup repairs or quarantines every declared partial durable state idempotently.
Crash and concurrency evidence satisfies the final L_RT promotion gate.
